content:
The article highlights a significant increase in public spending on private consultants, reaching £3.4 billion in 2023-24—a 62% rise since 2019-20. Despite post-pandemic expectations, spending remains elevated, posing a challenge for the new government, which aims to cut these costs by half. Recent contracts, including a £223 million deal with KPMG for civil service training, have drawn criticism. A Labour peer described the reliance on consultants as "scandalous," arguing they often provide little long-term value.
